args.body:
RED FLAGS REPORT
Due Diligence Review: Prairie Aerostructures Holdings
(aerospace vertical integration engagement)

CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT / PRIVILEGED

SCOPE & SOURCES
This report reviews the Prairie Aerostructures Holdings data room and flags red flags requiring escalation. It reconciles the counterparty's latest markup against the base deal materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal-team instruction. Sources reviewed: (1) deal materials (base agreement); (2) counterparty markup; (3) schedules and exhibits (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, Exhibit B); (4) deal team correspondence (latest controlling message). Administrative file 10 was identified as a misfiled distractor concerning an unrelated client engagement and was excluded.

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION
The latest, controlling message in the deal-team correspondence governs: the client will concede the indemnification basket conversion, but treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Superseded earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are disregarded.

SUMMARY
Four red flags require attention. One is a negotiated concession (the basket conversion). One is a firm walk-away threshold that the markup crosses (the survival-period reduction). Two are material risk-shifting deviations that must be quantified and negotiated down (the silent indemnification cap reduction and the MAE regulatory-action carve-out).

RED FLAG 1 — INDEMNIFICATION BASKET: DEDUCTIBLE CONVERTED TO TIPPING BASKET
The counterparty markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. Per the controlling deal instruction, the client has agreed to CONCEDE this conversion, so it is a known, accepted concession rather than a contested walk-away item. Flag it in the negotiating record as conceded but do not relitigate. NOTE: The concession must be read together with Red Flag 2; once in a tipping-basket structure the silent cap reduction below becomes more consequential.

RED FLAG 2 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP SILENTLY REDUCED (EScalate)
The markup silently reduces the indemnification cap. This is an adverse, un-announced tightening of the seller's exposure. Critically, Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would SILENTLY SHIFT to the client. The scheduled exceptions control over any general statements in the base materials. The silent cap reduction, combined with the retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2, materially shifts post-closing risk to the buyer. This must be quantified against Schedule 5.2 and the cap restored to the base deal level before signing.

RED FLAG 3 — MAE DEFINITION CARVE-OUT FOR REGULATORY ACTION (Escalate)
The markup adds a Material Adverse Effect (MAE) carve-out excluding regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue." Schedule 3.7 discloses TWO pending regulatory inquiries against Prairie Aerostructures. The carve-out would operate to strip MAE protection for precisely the two live regulatory matters, leaving the client without a walk-away or pricing remedy for the most material open risk in the deal. The scheduled exception (Schedule 3.7) controls and directly intersects this carve-out. This carve-out must be narrowed or removed so it does not carve out the two disclosed pending inquiries.

RED FLAG 4 — SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION — WALK-AWAY ISSUE (Blocker)
The markup shortens the survival period for the core representations via a new limitation period. Exhibit B sets the survival matrix, and the markup's limitation-period change DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS Exhibit B. Per the controlling deal instruction, any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue for the client. This is a hard blocker: do not accept any shortening of the survival period for the core representations. The markup must be conformed to Exhibit B. This is the single highest-priority red flag.

RECONCILIATION SUMMARY
- Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): CONCEDE per controlling instruction.
- Survival-period reduction: REJECT — walk-away issue (contradicts Exhibit B).
- Silent indemnification cap reduction + Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities: ESCALATE, restore cap.
- MAE carve-out for regulatory action + Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries: ESCALATE, narrow/remove carve-out.
- Distractor (admin file 10): EXCLUDED — unrelated, misfiled.

RECOMMENDED ACTIONS
1. Reject the survival-period reduction; keep the survival matrix per Exhibit B. Signal walk-away if not restored.
2. Restore the indemnification cap to the base level; quantify retained-liabilities shift from Schedule 5.2.
3. Narrow/remove the MAE regulatory-action carve-out so it does not cover the two Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries.
4. Record the basket-conversion concession in the deal terms sheet as accepted.
5. Do not rely on administrative file 10 (misfiled distractor).

The markup silently reduces the indemnification cap. This is an adverse, un-announced tightening of the seller's exposure. Critically, Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would SILENTLY SHIFT to the client. The scheduled exceptions control over any general statements in the base materials. The silent cap reduction, combined with the retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2, materially shifts post-closing risk to the buyer. This must be quantified against Schedule 5.2 and the cap restored to the base deal level before signing.

## RED FLAG 3 — MAE DEFINITION CARVE-OUT FOR REGULATORY ACTION (Escalate)
The markup adds a Material Adverse Effect (MAE) carve-out excluding regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue." Schedule 3.7 discloses TWO pending regulatory inquiries against Prairie Aerostructures. The carve-out would operate to strip MAE protection for precisely the two live regulatory matters, leaving the client without a walk-away or pricing remedy for the most material open risk in the deal. The scheduled exception (Schedule 3.7) controls and directly intersects this carve-out. This carve-out must be narrowed or removed so it does not carve out the two disclosed pending inquiries.

## RED FLAG 4 — SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION — WALK-AWAY ISSUE (Blocker)
The markup shortens the survival period for the core representations via a new limitation period. Exhibit B sets the survival matrix, and the markup's limitation-period change DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS Exhibit B. Per the controlling deal instruction, any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue for the client. This is a hard blocker: do not accept any shortening of the survival period for the core representations. The markup must be conformed to Exhibit B. This is the single highest-priority red flag.

## RECONCILIATION SUMMARY
- Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): CONCEDE per controlling instruction.
- Survival-period reduction: REJECT — walk-away issue (contradicts Exhibit B).
- Silent indemnification cap reduction + Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities: ESCALATE, restore cap.
- MAE carve-out for regulatory action + Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries: ESCALATE, narrow/remove carve-out.
- Distractor (admin file 10): EXCLUDED — unrelated, misfiled.

## RECOMMENDED ACTIONS
1. Reject the survival-period reduction; keep the survival matrix per Exhibit B. Signal walk-away if not restored.
2. Restore the indemnification cap to the base level; quantify retained-liabilities shift from Schedule 5.2.
3. Narrow/remove the MAE regulatory-action carve-out so it does not cover the two Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries.
4. Record the basket-conversion concession in the deal terms sheet as accepted.
5. Do not rely on administrative file 10 (misfiled distractor).
